Verified by observation on the paper FA master (DF8922141, port 4002, master clientId 0) 2026-07-23 pm. ### 2026-07-23 (main) — Afternoon paper FA tests (master clientId 0): per-subaccount execs, allocation methods, order lifecycle
Live on PAPER (port 4002) 2026-07-23 pm, connecting as the gateway MASTER API client id (clientId 0; OverrideTwsMasterClientID empty so 0 is default master). Reads only + place/modify/cancel of non-real orders. THREE findings.

FINDING 1 (settles #52) -- per-subaccount executions ARE visible to a master-connect FOR EQUITY BLOCKS, overturning the morning 'master-only, use Flex' conclusion (which was taken as non-master clientId 35). PROVEN on the PDBC equity block: DU8922143 and DU8922144 each surfaced their own 1-share Execution.acctNumber (execIds 0001106d.6a61995c.01.01 and .6a61995a.01.01); ExecutionFilter(acctCode=...) returned them individually. BUT INCOMPLETE: the SPY option combo AND all closing orders attributed only to FA master DF8922141 even as master with explicit acctCode filters -- no sub-account legs. NOT cache aging (surviving sub-account legs were the OLDEST fills). So: equity per-account execs API-visible via master-connect; options/combos/closes master-only -> complete per-account options trail still needs Flex/activity statements. reqPositions (not reqExecutions) is the reliable per-account allocation proof for equities too. IBKR_API_CURRENCY 3.2 upgraded hypothesis->VERIFIED-WITH-NUANCE.

FINDING 2 (resolves #50 architectural follow-up) -- a stable method removes the per-order replaceFA, WITH a decisive limitation. A Percent group (defaultMethod=Percent, 50/50) configured ONCE allocated BUY 4->2/2 and BUY 2->1/1 with ZERO replaceFA between orders. HOWEVER on ODD sizes Percent allocates EXACT FRACTIONAL shares: BUY 3->1.5/1.5, BUY 5->2.5/2.5 -- DISQUALIFYING for whole contracts (options). DECISION MATRIX: EQUAL/whole/stable -> EqualQuantity (odd-size rounding UNTESTED, new open item); UNEQUAL/fractional-ok (equity e.g. S0) -> Percent (stable, no rewrite); UNEQUAL/WHOLE contracts (options e.g. S8, the CRM brain's core case) -> ContractsOrShares ONLY, per-order amounts change -> per-order replaceFA STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED, not eliminable. CONSEQUENCE: the #50 replaceFA hot-path risk CANNOT be engineered away for the primary use case; manage it operationally (serialize, backup-before-write, read-back verify + fault-latch -- the 12 refinements). Does NOT reverse #50 (keep faGroup/replaceFA); explains WHY the write is unavoidable and points mitigation at ops.

FINDING 3 -- FA block modify/cancel lifecycle works (previously only place-and-fill proven). A resting DAY LIMIT FA block on a Percent group: placed (Submitted, orderId 174/permId 1979857105), MODIFIED to a new price (still Submitted, orderId AND permId both stable), CANCELLED (reached Cancelled, filled=0, gone from reqAllOpenOrders; IBKR error 202 = normal cancel ack). Nothing filled.

OPERATIONAL NOTE: reqPositions returns a stale snapshot if read immediately after a fill on a fresh master connection; a ~4-5s settle before reading resolves it. Monitoring that reads positions right after an order must include a settle delay or re-read.

Docs updated: CRM_DESIGN_groups_brain.md 13.7 (+13.6/10 refined), IBKR_API_CURRENCY.md 3.2 (+5 review log). No strategy/regime config touched.

### 2026-07-23 (main) — FA-allocation research resolves #50 (OrderAllocation is inbound-only) + corrects two same-day 'limitations' as test artifacts
Deep, adversarially-verified research 2026-07-23 (documentation + wire-protocol cross-checks; NO gateway, NO orders). Recorded to docs/IBKR_API_CURRENCY.md (new 3.9 + REVISED 3.1/3.2/3.5/3.8, 4 populated, review-log row) and docs/CRM_DESIGN_groups_brain.md 13.6 (resolved) + 10 item 5.

KEY FINDINGS. (1) OrderAllocation is INBOUND-only -- a class on OrderState the server returns to DESCRIBE an allocation (whatIf/order-preview + order state), added TWS API 10.33 / IBKR Campus changelog 2024-12-17; fields Account/Position/PositionDesired/PositionAfter/DesiredAllocQty/AllowedAllocQty/IsMonetary. It is NOT an outbound submission mechanism -- there is no 'attach OrderAllocation instead of replaceFA' path. Outbound allocation is still Order.faGroup/faMethod/faPercentage. Confirmed field-for-field by two independent wire-protocol ports (scmhub/ibapi Go, wboayue/rust-ibapi) + the Campus changelog. So #50 was largely a FALSE CHOICE. DECISION: keep faGroup/replaceFA for submission (current, documented, un-removed, ib_async 2.1.0 supports it). Do not switch libraries for a submission mechanism that does not exist. #50 CLOSED.

(2) The replaceFA hot-path risk is handled ARCHITECTURALLY: rewrite a group's XML only on MEMBERSHIP change, never per-order; serialize the writes. Per-order mutation exists only because ContractsOrShares encodes share counts as group config. Follow-up: evaluate whether a stable method / faPercentage removes per-order replaceFA without losing per-account control.

(3) TWO same-day 'known constraints' were TEST ARTIFACTS, corrected (REVISED, not overwritten): (a) per-subaccount reqExecutions ARE API-obtainable but receiving all clients' records needs the MASTER CLIENT ID; today used clientId 35, not master -- likely why we saw master-only records [API doc HIGH; clientId-35-is-why a STRONG HYPOTHESIS, NOT re-tested -> #52]. (b) whatIf per-account preview IS supported on 10.45.1g (accountsCount-length OrderAllocation array, gated by MIN_SERVER_VER_FULL_ORDER_PREVIEW_FIELDS); the hang was the ib_async whatIfOrder client bug (whatIf=True without transmit -> error 321 -> unresolved future), NOT an IBKR limit [HIGH] -> #53. Cross-ref #26/#48.

(4) No FA-allocation breaking changes in 2025 (10.35-10.42) or 2026 (10.43-10.48) production release notes; last FA-relevant change was 2022 v981/10.22 groups/profiles unification we are already on. CP Web API /iserver/account/allocation/* (Oct 2023) is group SETUP, not per-order submission.

Opened #52 (master-client-id reqExecutions re-test) and #53 (reach whatIf/OrderAllocation preview via ibapi or patched transmit).

TWO LIMITATIONS EXPOSED BY THE SAME SESSION (they change HOW we reconcile and pre-check, not WHETHER the architecture works):
(1) REPORTING -- IBKR returns allocation-order executions ONLY at the FA master. reqExecutions(ExecutionFilter(acctCode=...)) was run individually for all six managed accounts and returned records for DF8922141 ONLY, nothing for any DU subaccount. IBKR docs say per-subaccount reqExecutions should work; on this paper FA it returned nothing. Whether that is paper-FA-specific or general is UNCERTAIN (untested on a live FA). Treat the API as a dead end for per-account execution records: per-account proof must come from reqPositions + avgCost, or from a Flex/activity statement. Reconciliation is designed around positions + Flex.
(2) NO WHAT-IF / MARGIN-PREVIEW GATE for FA block orders. With transmit=True the FA master returns nothing at all for a group order (tested at 30s and 90s deadlines, zero error events); no IBKR doc claims whatIf support for allocation orders. Placing is the only way to validate a block. Any design assuming a what-if gate in front of a block is revised out; the margin/buying-power pre-check must be entirely self-computed from reqAccountSummary tags.

DOCUMENTED-LANGUAGE CONFIRMATIONS: faMethod="" is the DOCUMENTED path, not a workaround -- "If specifying actual group name and the faMethod is blank/omitted the default method of that group will be used" (interactivebrokers.github.io/tws-api/financial_advisor_methods_and_orders.html). ContractsOrShares is a PROFILE-style method, not one of the documented GROUP methods (EqualQuantity/NetLiq/AvailableEquity/PctChange); under TWS build 983+ "Use Account Groups with Allocation Methods" groups and profiles are unified -- requestFA/replaceFA accept Group only (Profile errors, which matches what fa_probe.py observed) and placeOrder accepts a profile name in faGroup (interactivebrokers.github.io/tws-api/financial_advisor.html). Also documented: "Unlike in TWS, there is not a default account allocation for the API -- it must be specified with every order placed."

### 2026-07-23 (main) — INCIDENT: paperbot arm restart killed the S8 LIVE-pilot Gateway on 4003 (2m51s outage)
`paperbot\arming.py arm` (paper-lane work: flip ReadOnlyApi=no for an FA group write) restarted the paper Gateway via the elevated GatewayArmRestart task, which ALSO killed the S8 live-pilot Gateway on port 4003 -- the instance CLAUDE.md marks NEVER touch.

OUTAGE 09:55:17 -> 09:58:08 CDT = 2m51s: lost live 0DTE collector data and BLIND exit-monitoring on a REAL funded account pilot. Recovered when Andrew manually ran LiveTradeGatewayOpen_0815CT (java pid 3496 bound 4003 at 09:58:08); collector resumed, monitor re-subscribed, 10:00 decision normal. PILOT_MODE zero-transmit wall NEVER breached -- no order placed, modified, or transmitted.

ROOT CAUSE (verified in code): connections/connections/gateway_watchdog.py:279 _kill_gateway_processes(port=PAPER_PORT, dir_substring=r'C:\IBC'). The PowerShell filter keeps a process if it owns the target port OR its CommandLine matches dir_substring (line 259). The PORT discriminator is correct and would have spared 4003; the DIRECTORY one is the bug -- C:\IBC is a string PREFIX of the sibling installs C:\IBC-Live-Data and C:\IBC-Live-Trade. The docstring at :281-283 claims it spares other instances on a different port/install dir -- that claim is FALSE for both siblings.

Undetected because: 4003 only exists since 2026-07-15 (clientids.py:23); the GatewayWatchdog task is Disabled; the paper call sites (gateway_arm_restart_elevated.py:77, gateway_watchdog.py:391) pass no args. Tests (test_gateway_watchdog.py:268-306) assert only on generated PowerShell TEXT, never on match semantics. And the arm wrote ok=true / detail=restarted-and-serving-data at 09:55:55 -- silent about the live gateway it had just destroyed.

IMPORTANT correction to the obvious fix: C:\IBC\ with a trailing separator spares the cmd.exe launchers but NOT the java JVMs -- all three lanes carry the shared classpath entry C:\IBC\IBC.jar, verified against the real running command lines. Discriminate on the per-instance config.ini / -DjtsConfigDir argument instead.

OPERATIONAL: arming.py arm AND disarm are both unsafe to run while any other Gateway is up until the fix lands (both go through restart_gateway(), arming.py:270 and :288). Triage discriminator is the CommandLine install dir via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -- NOT process start time (I initially mis-called live-trade pid 29236 a paper gateway on that basis, and corrected it).

Still open: fix = item #46; orphan java pid 29236 cleanup + the UNRESOLVED disappearance of the paper gateway on 4002 ~10:04 (cause not established) = item #47.
Full report: docs/INCIDENT_2026-07-23_arm_restart_killed_live_gateway.md

### 2026-07-20 (main) — S8 EXIT-LOGIC BUG found + fixed (e08568e) + restarted -- monitor was stopping on short leg alone, not the net spread
Andrew challenged the 24 same-day closes as implausible. Verified against the ACTUAL British IC dataset/research (not memory) and he was right: the exit monitor's stop trigger was faulty.

VERIFIED GROUND TRUTH (three primary sources): the S8 stop is a NET-SPREAD stop -- the position stops when the spread's mark-to-market COST TO CLOSE (short_ask - long_bid) rises to stop_price = PriceOpen(net credit) + StopMultiple. Sources: docs/S8_SPEC.md Sec 2.3 ('stopped when its mark-to-market cost to close rises to...'); british_ic/STRATEGY_MECHANICS.md Sec 4 (formula fit on 4,610 real rows, 99.98% exact, and it EXPLICITLY TESTED AND REJECTED any short-leg-price formula: 'PriceShort does not appear in the formula at all'); british_ic/stop_formula_verification.csv (PriceOpen = PriceShort - PriceLong = net credit, e.g. 4.12-0.17=3.95).

THE BUG: livebot/s8_monitor_core.py process_sample triggered on 'short_ask >= stop_price' -- the SHORT LEG ALONE, dropping the '- long_bid' term. Since the long leg always has value, short_ask alone is always well above the true spread cost, so the stop false-fired almost immediately after entry. PROVEN: all 24 of today's pre-fix stop_hits fired with the true spread cost (4.0-6.75) far below the 7.30 target -- every single one a false fire (0/24 legitimate). This is why there were 24 closes in two hours, all tiny losses, pnl approx equal to MAE, ~70s durations.

RECONCILES with Andrew's memory: the long LEG as a managed position has no closing metric of its own (per the B2 rule, S8_SPEC Sec 3, it just closes when the short stops -- no target/timer). But the long BID is a price component of the short position's stop metric (spread cost = short_ask - long_bid). Andrew drew exactly this distinction ('the long bid, not the long side of the trade'). The current code was missing that term.

FIX (commit e08568e, rule #1 clean -- stop_multiple/formula frozen and untouched, only the monitor's COMPARISON corrected to MATCH the spec): trigger now fires on (short_ask - long_bid) >= stop_price, via a shared spread_close_value() helper reused by pnl_at so trigger and P&L can never drift; missing either leg price -> no trigger, no crash. Corrected the module's own wrong docstring. Tests: full livebot suite 218 -> 221 green, incl. the incident-shape regression (short_ask=7.30/long_bid=2.95 -> cost 4.35 -> NO fire) which fails against the old code.

RESTARTED 10:49 CT to pick up the fix (service 20220->8372, collector 8532->1884; gateway untouched, no 2FA; orphans reaped cleanly). IMMEDIATE VINDICATION: the 18 resumed open positions, re-evaluated by the corrected logic against true net-spread cost with live ticks flowing 3+ min, are ALL HELD -- zero false stop_hits. The old process had been finalizing these same entries as stop_hit (10:00 -35, 10:40 -85, 10:50 -5); the new one correctly does not. Zero-transmit intact (PILOT_MODE=True on disk).

DATA IMPACT: every exit captured before 10:49 today is corrupt (false-fired). Entries are fine. Post-restart exits are the first trustworthy ones. NEXT: confirm afternoon slots capture (a) real net-spread stops only, (b) still one entry per grid slot (#36), (c) no Error 200 (#37). The #36/#37/#38 fixes remain confirmed; this stop bug is the 4th and most consequential live-test finding.

### 2026-07-20 (main) — S8 live-test defects #36/#37/#38 fixed + committed (2c203b8) -- code-complete, NOT yet proven live
All three defects found in the 2026-07-20 first live session are fixed, tested and committed as 2c203b8. Full livebot suite 218 passing (was 166). Zero-transmit untouched; no strategy/config knob changed (rule #1 clean).

#36 DUPLICATE ENTRIES was the arm-blocking one and WORSE than first logged. Not two duplicates -- the service re-entered the SAME grid slot on EVERY ~30s entry cycle across the whole +/-2min tolerance window. Live trades.jsonl: grid slot 08:45 produced FOUR entry batches (recorded slots 08:43/08:44/08:44/08:45) and 08:50 produced four, for BOTH Puts- and Calls-80-$4, where the strategy intended one each. ROOT CAUSE: s8_service.slot_already_entered queries the store by the ENTRY_GRID_CT LABEL while s8_capture derived TradeRecord.slot from the WALL-CLOCK entry timestamp -- the keys only coincide when a cycle lands exactly on the grid minute, so the guard never matched. FIX: thread the grid slot from s8_runner.evaluate_and_capture_due_template through capture_and_persist_entry into build_entry_trade_record, keying both TradeRecord.slot and trade_id; entry_ts keeps the true wall-clock instant; a missing slot falls back loudly, never silently.

#37 the ticket BLAMED THE WRONG COMPONENT. The collector log has ZERO Error 200s. The bad requests came from the ENTRY path's chain snapshot (s8_chain.build_0dte_chain), whose band comes off reqSecDefOptParams -- which returns the strike UNION across ALL SPX expirations, so 7805 exists for some expiry but not today's 0DTE. Also NO DATA WAS WASTED: _qualify already dropped the unresolved contracts, so the chain was always correct and the entire cost was log noise. FIX: filter the band to strikes actually listed for the expiry (one cached reqContractDetails per expiry); band width unchanged, entry path sees an identical contract set.

#38 the email failsafe FIRED AND WAS DELIVERED in the real 08:28 outage (that part passed). The UNKNOWN field was because the error string was NEVER CAPTURED: both call sites detect the drop by POLLING ib.isConnected(), which raises no exception, while ib_async's client.apiError carried 'Peer closed connection.' with nothing subscribed. FIX: a disconnect recorder subscribes to apiError so the real string reaches the body verbatim; when genuinely unavailable the body names what was checked and came up empty. New WHAT HAPPENED block classifies state from the JVM-alive + port probes, so 'JVM alive YES / port 4003 YES' alongside a drop now reads as 'API session dropped, gateway process stayed up' instead of a contradiction.

PROCESS LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the #36 worker reported the fix complete but had been interrupted mid-edit and left 'if False:' in the fallback guard -- the entire fix was a no-op while the diff looked finished. Its own regression test caught it (216 passed / 2 failed). Running the suite, not trusting the report, is what caught it.

RETRACTED THIS SESSION: an earlier claim that the live processes run under system Python instead of the venv was WRONG. ### 2026-07-18 (main) — data_backup: fix nightly false-page defect found by the first real verification
The first real 99 GB data backup completed and VERIFIED on 2026-07-18: 499,539 files / 104.2 GiB copied, rclone copy exit 0, and rclone check confirmed 499,534 files byte-identical (md5) with ZERO .parquet mismatches. The irreplaceable warehouse now has a proven off-machine copy.

But the follow-up rclone check --one-way --checksum exited 1 with 17 differences found / 17 errors while checking / 9 files missing. Every one was benign live-file churn; zero corruption.

The exact breakdown:
- 9 "file not in Google drive root": all under s8_pilot/logs/, a directory a CONCURRENT S8 session created at 15:35, roughly four hours AFTER the backup started at 11:17. rclone cannot copy a file that did not exist when it walked that path.
- 8 "sizes differ", i.e. files that changed between copy time and check time: conductor/conductor.db (written continuously all session), warehouse/heartbeat_alarm.log, warehouse/morning_execute.log, warehouse/register_forward_live.ps1, warehouse/run_forward_live.bat, state/paperbot/paperbot.log, state/paperbot/runs.jsonl, warehouse/raw/options/_manifest.json.

THE DEFECT this exposed: data_backup.py as built treated ANY check difference as failure. Those same files churn every single day, so DataBackupDaily would have failed its check EVERY NIGHT, left the heartbeat cold, and paged. A false-page generator - exactly the alarm-fatigue failure this quarter's work (see #29, #33 and the repo_backup history) exists to eliminate. It was found only by actually running the verification against real data, not by reading the code.

THE FIX - classify differences into three tiers, never blanket-ignore them:
- TIER 1, PRECIOUS/IMMUTABLE, hard failure and page: anything under warehouse/raw/** (write-once historical market data) except the manifest/index sidecars. Also tier 1: a file missing from the remote whose local mtime is OLDER than the run start (it existed when rclone walked, so it should have been copied and was not); any "hashes could not be checked"; any difference matching no known-volatile pattern; any unrecognised reason; and any reported problem that no per-file ERROR line accounts for. Tier 1 MUST still fail closed, because the entire purpose of this job is that a real corruption of irreplaceable data pages loudly - forgiving the noise must never cost us the signal. *.parquet is deliberately excluded from the volatile list.
- TIER 2, KNOWN-VOLATILE, recorded but does not fail: an explicit, commented pattern list derived from the 8 real observations plus obvious siblings (*.log, *.jsonl, *.db and the sqlite -wal/-shm sidecars, *_manifest.json, *heartbeat*, *_progress*.json, *_state.json, *.lock, s8_pilot/logs/*, and the two observed warehouse scripts by exact path).
- TIER 3, CREATED DURING THE RUN, recorded but does not fail: missing on the remote AND local mtime newer than the run-start timestamp captured before rclone launched. It gets copied on the next run.

The heartbeat now refreshes only when there are zero tier-1 failures, so benign churn no longer blocks a legitimately good backup. Benign items are recorded in the status JSON under benign_differences with counts and a capped sample plus the reason each was forgiven, and the proves string NAMES them - it never implies a clean 100% when there were benign differences, and never hides a tier-1 failure.

Tests: test_data_backup.py went 26 -> 50 passing, including a tier-1 parquet mismatch that must still hard-fail with a cold heartbeat, a mixed case where benign churn must not mask a real failure, and a verbatim replay of the real 17 differences that must NOT page. Full datacollector package: 271 passing (was 241).

Item #31 (register the DataBackupDaily scheduled task) was DELIBERATELY HELD until this fix landed - registering the job as built would have wired up a nightly false page.

copy-not-sync is DELIBERATE: `copy` is additive and NEVER deletes on the remote, so a local deletion / corruption / bug can never propagate to and nuke the only spare copy. `sync` would mirror destruction into the backup and call it success.

Cadence<->threshold coupling (documented in both register_data_backup_task.ps1 and heartbeat_alarm.py): 30h = 24h daily cadence + ~6h grace for a long run. Change the schedule -> change the threshold, or it false-pages (too tight) or sleeps through an outage (too loose).

### 2026-07-17 (main) — infra: Drive-sync tripwire — pages if TradingDesk-Local ever comes under Drive management
Built a Drive-sync TRIPWIRE that pages the moment C:\TradingDesk-Local (the ~99 GB
irreplaceable market-data + secrets + venv folder) comes under Google Drive
sync/backup/mirror management.

WHY (the human residual risk): TradingDesk-Local is deliberately OFF Drive because
Drive's sync client corrupts market data and once silently synced the WRONG FOLDER
for 9 days (2026-07-07..16). We are now backing the REPO up to Drive via rclone
(explicit checksummed API uploads — safe) which does NOT put TradingDesk-Local under
the Drive Desktop sync client. The leftover risk is purely human: someone later opens
Google Drive Desktop and adds C:\TradingDesk-Local (or a subfolder, or an ancestor)
to sync/mirror/backup, re-arming the exact bomb. This converts "everyone must remember
never to" into "you get paged the moment anyone does."

WHAT IT DETECTS (investigated on the live machine first, honestly):
- THREAT 1 (mirror/streaming — tree ends up UNDER a DriveFS volume): RELIABLY
  detectable. Reuses repo_backup.is_drive_managed() (OS volume mount-root + 'Google
  Drive' label test). Verified: every protected path currently resolves to the SYSTEM
  volume (healthy).
- THREAT 2 (folder backup / mirror-of-a-local-folder — files stay local, so a volume
  test does NOT catch it; this is the dangerous wrong-folder shape): detectable via
  DriveFS's own registry. root_preference_sqlite.db `roots` table carries root_path +
  last_seen_absolute_path (full absolute local paths); mirror_sqlite.db mirror_item /
  root_config corroborate. Measured today: 0 rows (clean streaming install) = the
  healthy baseline. The tripwire flags ANY registered local root overlapping the tree
  (equal / ancestor / descendant), so it does not need to distinguish backup-vs-mirror
  sync_type. An UNRELATED backup root does NOT false-page.
- PROXY (positive-only): shallow scan for NTFS reparse-point/placeholder attrs and
  Drive transfer temp dirs (.tmp.drivedownload/.tmp.driveupload). A hit pages; absence
  proves nothing and never contributes to green.

HONEST LIMIT: the THREAT-2 registry tables are EMPTY right now, so the overlap-match
logic has NOT been exercised against a real populated backup row on this machine. The
column semantics are self-evident and match repo_backup's existing use of `roots`, but
a future Drive-client schema change (or a backup recorded only in a form whose path we
don't recognise) could be missed by the DB read alone. That gap is exactly why the
tripwire does not rely on the DB alone — it also runs THREAT 1 and the schema-independent
proxy, and it fails closed rather than silently passing when it cannot read the registry.
Also noted: one transient read of root_preference_sqlite.db showed only max_ids (a
mid-write/WAL flicker); re-reads were stable. Handled by fail-closed + the 3h cooldown.

FAIL-OPEN vs FAIL-CLOSED (deliberate): the tripwire FAILS CLOSED. A check that
affirmatively finds a threat pages the remediation; a check that CANNOT be evaluated
(DriveFS installed but its registry DB unreadable / the volume mount root
undeterminable / the tripwire module failed to import) ALSO pages, with "could not
evaluate" wording. The single safe exception: if DriveFS is not installed at all, the
registry checks are trivially clean (nothing could be managing the tree). A guard that
goes silent when it can't look is the exact silent failure this whole body of work
exists to kill.

READS GREEN TODAY: live run exits 0 (threat1 clean / threat2 0-rows / proxy clean).
If it paged in the current healthy state it would be worthless.

INTEGRATION: new stdlib-only module datacollector/drive_sync_tripwire.py (imports
repo_backup for the DriveFS helpers, exactly as heartbeat_alarm already does).
heartbeat_alarm.py evaluates it every 15-min sweep via a new handle_tripwire() — a
STATE ASSERTION, not a staleness/heartbeat job — reusing the same _send() path and 3h
cooldown de-dupe. No new scheduled task. Tests: test_drive_sync_tripwire.py (29,
including a live-green assertion, THREAT-1/THREAT-2 trips, unreadable-registry
fail-closed, and the page naming the folder + remediation). Full datacollector suite
215 passing. This makes the "never touch the sync client for TradingDesk-Local" rule
LOUD instead of discipline-only.

### 2026-07-17 (main) — CORRECTION: entry #32's "parentId is immediately consistent" claim was FALSE
Retracts the mechanism claimed in conductor entry #32 and in commit 8a07993's message. Both remain in the history unamended -- this entry is the correction, per the never-rewrite-history rule. Simplification shipped in the accompanying commit.

THE FALSE CLAIM: entry #32 and 8a07993 assert that Drive's NAME INDEX is eventually consistent (lagging 3-5 minutes) while a parentId listing is IMMEDIATELY consistent, and that this made the name-query lookup a false-page generator on healthy backups. The "parentId is immediate" half is FALSE and the false-page framing rests on it.

THE ACTUAL DATA. Bundle tradingdesk-repo-20260716-162242.bundle, written 16:22:42: title query EMPTY at ~16:23 and ~16:25; parentId listing FOUND at ~16:27; title query FOUND at ~16:27, moments after. Bundle tradingdesk-repo-20260716-163838.bundle, written 16:38:38: parentId listing NOT FOUND at ~16:40 (it still showed 162242 as newest); title query FOUND at ~16:41; parentId listing FOUND at ~16:42. On the second bundle the NAME QUERY FOUND THE FILE BEFORE THE PARENT LISTING DID -- the opposite of the claim.

THE ERROR: parentId was observed succeeding at 16:27 and called "immediate", when five minutes had already elapsed since the 16:22:42 write. The title query succeeded moments later and that was misread as "the index caught up" rather than the simpler reading -- that BOTH were waiting on the same lag. A mechanism was attributed to query type when the only variable that actually differed was elapsed time. Three observations, confounded timing, asserted confidently, and labelled "the most important finding of the session."

WHAT IS TRUE AND MAY BE ASSERTED: Drive's API lags the local write by roughly 1-5 minutes REGARDLESS of query type. That lag is real, was measured, and is the genuine finding -- it is what makes the bounded 300s poll essential rather than optional. The poll was added unprompted during the 742e9a6 build for the right instinct and better reasons than were later given for it. The md5 reasoning is untouched and stands on its own: a metadata hit proves a row exists, not that bytes landed, because Drive computes md5Checksum server-side only after content arrives.

HONEST LIMIT ON EVEN THE TRUE PART: the lag was measured through this session's MCP Drive connector, not through the raw endpoint repo_backup.py calls. The connector's title operator probably maps onto name in files.list, but that is not proven. n=2 bundles.

WHAT CHANGED IN CODE: the lookup is simplified back to a SINGLE parent-scoped name query -- q=name='<bundle>' and '<folder_id>' in parents and trashed=false. The paginated full-folder listing and client-side filename matching are gone; they existed only to serve the false claim, and they bought real complexity plus a new failure mode in the repo's most safety-critical script for a benefit that does not exist.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY KEPT, and why it is NOT part of the retraction: folder-id resolution and parent-scoping STAY. The 2026-07-07..16 incident was Drive syncing the WRONG FOLDER. A check asking only "does a file with this name and md5 exist SOMEWHERE in the Drive" would have PASSED throughout that incident. Folder identity is precisely what has to be verified here. The folder id is resolved, never hardcoded. Also kept: the bounded poll (now better justified than before), md5 as the real proof, absent-md5 as a keep-polling state, folder-resolution failure as a distinct note with no silent fallback to an unscoped query, and fail-closed semantics. CLOUD_VERIFY_REQUIRED remains False; #29 is still blocked on Andrew's GCP setup.

THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the false claim was produced by the same habit the desk exists to prevent -- reading a confirming result and stopping, instead of asking what else explains it. It was caught only because a second bundle was observed, and the second observation was made by accident. Two data points, not one, before a mechanism gets asserted into the compliance record.

### 2026-07-16 (main) — repo_backup: Drive's name index is eventually consistent -- it was a false-page generator
Found 2026-07-16 by RUNNING the thing, not by inspection. Fixed in 8a07993. This is the most important finding of the session and the reason to keep observing real behaviour rather than trusting a design.

WHAT HAPPENED: after wiring wrap-triggered backup, a real --wrap run produced tradingdesk-repo-20260716-162242.bundle at 16:22:42 local. Google recorded it with createdTime 2026-07-16T21:22:42.976Z and fileSize 41657962 -- an exact match to the local file, uploaded essentially instantly. But a title/name-based Drive search returned EMPTY at ~16:23 and again at ~16:25. The identical query returned the file at ~16:27. The file was present in Drive the WHOLE time. Only the NAME INDEX lagged, roughly 3-5 minutes. A parentId listing of the backups folder returned the file IMMEDIATELY and accurately at a moment when the name query was still empty.

WHY IT MATTERED: verify_cloud_arrival() as shipped in 742e9a6 located the bundle with q=name='<bundle>' and trashed=false. That races the name INDEX, not the upload. On a perfectly healthy backup the check would report "not in the cloud", fail closed, and page. A false page on a healthy backup is exactly how a pager gets ignored -- which is the mechanism behind the 9-day Drive silence (2026-07-07..16) that this entire body of work exists to prevent. It would also have been intermittent, presenting as a flaky network. The bounded 300s poll would have masked it on fast days and failed on slow ones: worse than a clean failure, because it would have been trusted.

THE FIX (8a07993): locate the bundle by LISTING THE PARENT FOLDER and matching the filename client-side. _drive_find (name query) deleted outright, no callers left. New: _drive_list_children (parentId listing, paginated to exhaustion, capped at 50 pages), _drive_path_components, _drive_resolve_folder_id (walks My Drive matching each component client-side, so no step touches the lagging index). The folder id is RESOLVED, never hardcoded -- the observed id 1ppfS44BaR25_TnD8WT6g8vqwCAjKbTGA is this machine's current folder and hardcoding it would be a landmine if the folder were ever recreated. Folder-resolution failure produces a distinct honest note and does NOT silently fall back to a name query (a test asserts the list function is never called after such a failure). The pagination cap returns None -- failure to enumerate -- never a short list, because a truncated listing would be a false page in new clothes, the same bug in a new place.

MD5 REMAINS THE REAL PROOF, and this finding is a second independent argument for it: a parentId hit proves a metadata row exists, NOT that the bytes landed. Drive computes md5Checksum server-side only AFTER content arrives. So an absent md5Checksum on a found file is now an explicit keep-polling state -- not success, not failure -- and a poll timeout in that state produces a note distinguishing "registered but content not landed" from "absent". The poll now waits on the upload rather than on an index, which is what it was always supposed to do.

HONEST LIMIT: the lag was measured through this session's MCP Drive connector, whose title operator very probably maps onto the same name field in files.list, but that is NOT proven for the raw endpoint repo_backup.py calls. No comment or commit claims otherwise. Listing the parent is defensively correct regardless of which layer lagged, is strictly more reliable, and costs nothing.

BUG CAUGHT INSIDE THE FIX, by tests rather than inspection: the first prefix check used len(dparts) > len(mparts), making the "dest IS the mount root" branch unreachable -- it would have reported the right failure for the WRONG REASON. A wrong-reason note is precisely the failure class this module exists to kill, and it nearly shipped inside the fix for it. Caught by test_path_components_refuse_when_the_dest_is_the_mount_itself.

TESTS: test_repo_backup.py 115 -> 144 passing; package 154 -> 183 (with the two known-broken files ignored). CLOUD_VERIFY_REQUIRED still False -- all of this is still inert until Andrew completes the GCP setup on #29.

### 2026-07-16 (main) — infra: wrap now triggers a verified backup; HEAD-unchanged skip; 20:00 stays the net
Andrew's call 2026-07-16, built in bca6db6. THE GAP: wrap (CLAUDE.md's force-word) ran the conductor sweep and stopped -- it never backed anything up. Backups fired only via RepoBackupDaily (20:00 + AtLogon). So a wrap at 15:00 followed by a disk failure at 19:00 lost the day: the 20:00 job never ran. The moment Andrew declares a coherent stopping point is exactly when the work is most worth archiving, and nothing used it. Nobody had built it; there was no better reason than that.

DESIGN -- BOTH, NOT EITHER. Wrap-triggered backup is primary (captures the good state the instant it exists). RepoBackupDaily STAYS as the safety net, deliberately: Andrew does not always wrap (he said so -- there are days he walks away without closing a session, and those are precisely the days the net matters), and the daily cadence is what feeds heartbeat_alarm.py's 26h staleness check. Wrap-only would false-page every quiet weekend. The task's existing AtLogon trigger already partly covers the walk-away case.

SHIPPED: (1) --wrap mode + run_repo_backup_wrap.cmd -- same fail-closed contract as the scheduled path, but prints human progress (it runs while Andrew waits) and emits a compact single-line JSON summary as its last stdout line so the session can report the outcome without parsing the status file. It still does NOT commit -- committing is the session's job; the backup stays read-only w.r.t. git. (2) HEAD-unchanged skip + --force to bypass. (3) 39 new tests, test_repo_backup.py 76 -> 115, package 115 -> 154 passing, no regressions.

WHY THE SKIP: today's three bundles all carried head_sha b50e78b -- identical HEAD, all three redundant, ~41MB each. Once wrap triggers backups that churn multiplies and KEEP_LAST=7 starts evicting genuinely distinct history in favour of duplicates.

THE SKIP READS THE BUNDLE, NOT THE STATUS FILE. It gets HEAD via git bundle list-heads on the artifact itself rather than trusting the last run's recorded head_sha -- reading the status file would inherit a PREVIOUS RUN'S BELIEF, which is the same second-hand-claim pattern that let Drive lie for 9 days. Both copies (local and Drive) are interrogated separately: same name is not same file. It errs toward bundling -- if the prior bundle is missing, fails verification, or its head cannot be read, it does NOT skip, it bundles fresh. Skip happens only on affirmative proof the existing bundle is good AND current. The skip refreshes the heartbeat, which is correct: a verified current off-machine bundle genuinely exists, and that is the only thing the heartbeat has ever asserted. The re-verify is real work (it rescans both copies every run), so a bundle Drive lost or corrupted fails to skip and gets rebuilt -- staleness cannot hide behind it.

HOLE FOUND AND CLOSED DURING THE BUILD: a skip that bypassed the cloud check would have meant that flipping CLOUD_VERIFY_REQUIRED to True later would silently NOT apply to the majority of runs -- the check would look enforced while mostly not running. A skip now runs the same cloud check against the bundle it leans on, with the same fail-closed decision. CLOUD_VERIFY_REQUIRED stays False; the unattended OAuth path from 742e9a6 is untouched and still blocked on Andrew's GCP setup (#29).

ALSO FIXED: CLAUDE.md's "Where things live" pointed at connections\clientids.py; the real path is connections\connections\clientids.py (nested package). conductor/db.py:6 had it right. Andrew approved.

KNOWN, PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED: bare pytest -q in datacollector EXITS 2 on collection errors -- ibkr_option_stream_test.py and ibkr_stream_test.py are standalone scripts that run int(sys.argv[1]) at import, so pytest's own -q flag crashes them at collection. Reproduced before any of today's changes; unrelated to this work. It means datacollector has no working one-command test run: the 115/154 figures are with those two files --ignore'd. They are scripts wearing _test.py names. Needs a deliberate fix (rename, or a pytest config ignore) -- not done, not Andrew-blocked, just out of scope today.

### 2026-07-13 (main) — July 9 ThetaData backfill closed + rebuild_catalog() production bug found/fixed (4 bugs)
Closes #22 (missing 2026-07-09 ThetaData options-chain snapshot). Data collection succeeded early (all 50 roots, verified on disk), but closing this out required chasing a real pre-existing production bug in datacollector/storage.py's rebuild_catalog() -- the backfill script's final step, called after every one-off backfill and by the nightly ThetaEodDaily job.

Four distinct bugs found and fixed in sequence, each only surfacing after fixing the last:
1. Original: rebuild_catalog() embedded all ~312k warehouse file paths as one literal SQL array in a single CREATE VIEW ... read_parquet(..., union_by_name=true) statement. Confirmed via real benchmarks (2k/20k/100k file scales) to scale superlinearly -- killed after 52 min with no completion against the real 311,988-file warehouse. (Matches a prior undiagnosed symptom: a 2026-06-27 commit message already noted this function 'hard-crashing the interpreter' at ~102k files -- same root cause, never fixed until now.)
2. Fix attempt 1 (chunking into bounded ~5,000-file views) hit a second bug: the manifest-table bulk write used con.executemany() to upsert ~312k rows one at a time -- killed after 46+ min with no completion.
3. Fix attempt 2 (bulk DataFrame-backed insert) surfaced a resume-robustness gap: a kill between the manifest commit and the per-chunk view-build loop could leave some chunk views un-built with no way to detect it on a later no-op call. Fixed by detecting chunks whose _catalog_chunks row has no live view.
4. The real remaining wall (not anticipated going in): UNION ALL BY NAME over many chunk views is NOT cheap regardless of file count -- DuckDB re-binds each chunk's full read_parquet(union_by_name=true) definition on every reference, compounding to ~O(n^2) in chunk count (measured 4s/10s/34s/140s at 2/4/8/16 chunks). Fixed by forcing one consistent schema across all chunks up front (an explicit read_parquet(schema=...) derived from a representative file, forcing the real open_interest double/int64 type drift found during diagnosis to DOUBLE in both file orderings), so the union becomes plain positional UNION ALL -- confirmed linear (0.29s @ 16 chunks vs 140s before).

Real measured result: full bootstrap rebuild against the actual 311,988-file warehouse now takes 16.9 seconds (was: never completes). Independently verified (not just taken on faith): queried the rebuilt catalog directly and confirmed 187,298 rows for 2026-07-09 across exactly 50 roots; ran the datacollector test suite myself (39 passed, 2 pre-existing unrelated argv-script collection errors, confirmed not caused by this change); confirmed both commits exist and no orphaned processes were left running.

Commits: 40b4a30 (storage.py fix + test_storage.py), ada471c (backfill_20260709.py, one-off script committed for the record, same convention as backfill_20260626.py).

### 2026-07-10 (s8-simulator-abort-2026-07-10) — S8 mechanical simulator: root cause isolated via real-trade replication, then ABORTED by Andrew; pivoted same session to regime-bucketing the known real window
Followed up on open item #18 (mechanical simulator FAILED calibration). Built a deterministic replication test: replayed all 1,222 strict TAT-matched REAL trades (real date+time+template, no invented schedule) through the simulator's per-trade engine and diffed simulated vs real strike/credit/P&L. Findings, in order isolated: (1) strike selection accurate (median ~5pt diff both legs). (2) settlement-trade P&L accurate (mean diff +$70/trade, matches real 79.4% win rate on that subset). (3) B2/long-leg-policy confound RULED OUT -- reran short-leg-only (real short_fifo_pnl vs sim short-leg mechanics, ignoring the long leg entirely, since B2 does not touch the short leg) and got nearly the identical aggregate gap as the whole-position comparison (+$41,202 real vs -$43,734 sim), so B2 diverging from real long-leg handling was never the driver. (4) warehouse data quality RULED OUT -- cross-checked the two most extreme stop-exit mismatches (2026-03-09, 2025-10-14) against the underlying spot-estimate path AND 4 neighboring strikes at the same minute; both moves were coherent across strikes and correlated with a genuine spot move, not isolated bad ticks. (5) stop-trigger CLASSIFICATION is accurate -- 94.8% of the 503 trades the simulator flagged as 'stop' really were real losers (mean real loss -$243/contract on that group). (6) The isolated remaining bug: stop-exit FILL MAGNITUDE on those correctly-classified trades runs ~2.1x too punishing (sim mean -$508 vs real mean -$243 on the same 503 trades). The 13.6x-half-spread slippage constant's aggregate median roughly matches real data (13.79x measured), so the gap likely comes from applying that multiplier at the exact stressed trigger-minute (when the half-spread is itself already elevated) rather than the constant's central value being wrong -- not fully resolved, two candidate explanations (fill-price-at-stress-moment vs trigger-timing precision) were left unpicked. Andrew's call at that point: ABORT the mechanical-simulator/2022-2026-extension approach entirely, not fix-and-continue. Rationale: every component (spot estimate, strike selection, entry timing, fill model) has only ever been checked against the ONE period with real ground truth (2025-2026) -- even a fixed version extending trust to genuinely novel years (2022-2024) would be an unverifiable leap, a curve-fit risk baked into the whole approach, not just this one bug. Session cost (hours of diagnostic chasing) was also disproportionate to the payoff. Pivoted same session to a much cheaper test of the same underlying worry (is S8's edge concentrated in one type of day): regime-bucketed the REAL known 236-day window using S0's EXISTING FROZEN regime engine (strategies/parts/regime.py -- market_health_score + apply_hysteresis, no new thresholds) joined to the already-existing real daily P&L series (british_ic/alpha_vs_beta_daily_series.csv, built in an earlier session). Zero synthetic execution -- no strike selection, no fill model, no spot estimation. Result: S8 profitable in 4 of 5 regime buckets, covering 212 of 236 days (90%) -- RiskOn +$69,077/101d, RiskOnNarrowing +$64,894/89d, Defensive +$6,104/12d, CapitalPreservation +$8,358/10d (highest per-day mean of any bucket -- the tail-hedge thesis holding up, not just one lucky crash day). One real soft spot: Caution regime, -$9,450/24d. Totals reconcile exactly to the previously-published headline (+$138,981 computed vs +$138,982 documented; +$42,765 actual matches exactly), a strong sanity check the daily series and join are correct. Caveat: extreme-regime buckets are thin (n=10-12) -- this shows the edge isn't fragile to the regime diversity that occurred WITHIN the one known year, it does not prove survival of a genuine multi-year bear or 2008-style event. Left uncommitted: british_ic/s8_mechanical_simulator.py + SIMULATOR_STAGE_B_PROGRESS.md (prior session's probability-fix attempt, now moot given the abort decision) and 3 new untracked diagnostic scripts (s8_replication_test.py, s8_short_leg_only_diag.py, s8_real_slippage_check.py) documenting this session's isolation work -- not committed, Andrew's call whether to preserve for the record or discard.

rebuild), 044d93e (Stage-B template comment polish), ed6ff50 (29x performance fix), 501dc24
(calibration-compare + extended-run scripts).

Calibration against the KNOWN 2025-2026 real window (the only way to sanity-check before trusting
the simulator on 2022-2024 where there's no ground truth) came back badly wrong. First attempt:
-$1,440,129 total sim P&L vs the real account's +$138,982 -- traced to entries firing 7x too often
per day (76.5/day vs real 11.0/day) because a schedule-derivation step treated "this time-slot
appeared on X% of historical days" as "fires every day" instead of "fires with probability X%."
Fixed (converted to a real per-slot empirical firing probability, deterministically seeded per
date/template/slot) and re-run on the full 247-day window: trade frequency improved a lot
(15.1/day, much closer to real 11.0/day) but total P&L was STILL negative (-$233,203 vs the real
+$138,982) and the stop rate barely moved (39.8% vs the original 40.4%) -- the frequency fix was
real and necessary but not sufficient; a deeper, still-undiagnosed mismatch remains.

Late in the session Andrew corrected a wrong assumption that had been driving the diagnosis: the
TAT system is a FULLY AUTOMATED algorithmic program (not a human making daily discretionary calls),
which means the real explanation for why any given scheduled slot only fires on 73-85% of its
"eligible" days is a discoverable MECHANICAL rule (an IV filter, a capital/position constraint,
something in the data) -- not human judgment, and not something to model as a random probability
draw the way the fix did. This reframes the whole failure: the probability-weighted-draw fix was
itself likely the wrong model, not just an incomplete one. A further open question, never
resolved: whether the SAME automated system also controls the long leg's exit (in which case "B2"
isn't a proposed correction, it's us discovering an already-existing real rule we haven't correctly
identified) or whether the long-leg exit is a separate/different process (in which case the
existing B2 characterization stands). Session ended here at Andrew's request to stop and wrap up,
without resolving this. See conductor items #18 (simulator) and #19 (long-leg-exit question).
